text:
The Sarpy Creek Basin, including Tracts II and III, is a relatively poor area for pronghorn production (Martin, 1975). For the period January-December, 1975, 222 pronghorn observations were recorded on the leases. Population estimates of 20 (Tract II) and 14 (Tract III) have been made (Westmoreland Resources 1975 o). Pronghorns have been observed in the Project Area from April to November; the herd apparently moves to more suitable habitat during the winter months. Lack of adequate winter range in the lease area has been cited as the reason for these seasonal movements (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 o). Martin (1975) states that large areas of relatively flat land covered with sagebrush are necessary for good pronghorn winter range.
Habitat type usage by pronghorns varied in Tracts II and III.

Silver sagebrush - grasslands were used heavily on Tract II while antelope of Tract III prefered grasslands over other habitat types; big sagebrush and sagebrush - grasslands were second in importance (Westmoreland 1975 o).
The only predatory mammal of significant economic importance which has been observed in relatively large numbers is the coyote. The coyote has recently been the object of much concern due to its high reproductive rate and large populations, its predatory nature and high prices paid for its fur (up to $60 in 1975). Coyotes have been observed in nearly all habitat types on the Project Area. Other predators observed in the area include the raccoon, striped skunk and bobcat. The bobcat, although it is present in very limited numbers, is of considerable furbearing value, with 1975 prices in excess of $100.
